key_insight: This paper presents the first system that synthesizes synchronized, full 3D facial animations for two co-located speakers from a single mixed audio stream by explicitly modeling their relative 3D spatial relationship (position, orientation, mutual gaze).
problem_solved: Generates realistic in-person multi-speaker 3D conversations from mixed audio—moving beyond disembodied 'talking heads' by resolving who speaks when and how speakers orient, look, and react to each other in space.
method: Separate and attribute mixed audio to individual participants (speaker diarization/voice separation) and extract conversational cues (turns, prosody).
Predict per-speaker 3D head pose, facial expression, and gaze conditioned on the separated audio plus a learned interaction module that models relative position/orientation and mutual gaze dynamics.
Render synchronized 3D performances for both participants in a shared spatial scene, ensuring temporal consistency and cross-participant responses.
impact: Enables realistic multi-person avatars for AR/VR, telepresence, social robotics, and human behavior research by producing spatially coherent, interactive 3D conversations from audio alone—improving realism and social signal fidelity over single-head methods.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: mixed audio -> audio separation/diarization -> interaction module -> per-speaker 3D animation
Before/After comparison: side-by-side of conventional talking-head outputs vs. co-located 3D conversation with correct orientations and mutual gaze
Spatial schematic: top-down view showing relative positions, orientation vectors, and gaze lines between participants
Timeline visualization: audio waveform aligned with speaker turns and synthesized facial/head motion keyframes
paper_title: Talking Together: Synthesizing Co-Located 3D Conversations from Audio
paper_authors: Mengyi Shan, Shouchieh Chang, Ziqian Bai, Shichen Liu, Yinda Zhang
